profile_text.body:
TalkingPoints is a nonprofit that describes its platform as the only PreK-12 family engagement platform purpose-built to make partnership easy, inclusive, and impactful. According to its site, the research-based platform is built on the practices of Universal Family Engagement, an approach it says weaves trust and partnership into the everyday rhythm of school life, with the goal of improving student attendance, behavior, well-being, and academic outcomes. The site presents case material from districts and schools including East [ECISD], Fairfax County Public Schools, Eden Prairie Schools in Minnesota, Esperanza Cyber Charter School, and Putnam City Schools in Oklahoma City.

Its tracked product is also named TalkingPoints, listed under Education and Research AI. The product provides translation in more than 100 languages, described as human plus machine, and is aimed at teachers, administrators, and families. It is family-facing, with no student accounts needed. The paid school and district version syncs contacts from the student information system, and a Common Sense privacy rating is not yet published. It is free for teachers in the United States and Canada, with paid school and district plans; a third party reported the free tier as up to 200 students and 5 classes.

The site's content is largely district stories and staff-written pieces, including accounts from Shane McKay, Assistant Superintendent for East [ECISD], Alanna Dushok of Fairfax County Public Schools, Ingrid Parker-Hill, Michelle Thompson, Luis Franco, and Carrie Rogers, Aditi Kumari of Eden Prairie Schools, and Principal Melissa Molina of Esperanza Cyber Charter School. No litigation, MCP servers, or SEC or patent facts are recorded for the organization.
